claims.claim: Psychology is the scientific study of the mind and behavior (the APA working definition).
Psychology emerged from philosophy and became an empirical science.
Psychology became its own academic discipline only in the late 1800s.
The mind refers to inner experience: thoughts, feelings, perceptions, memories, attention, and other mental activity.
Behavior refers to an organism's activities in response to internal or external stimuli, including actions others can observe.
Psychologists acquire knowledge through systematic observation, experimentation, testing, and analysis rather than intuition or authority alone.
Science works with what is perceivable and measurable; untestable claims fall outside its reach.
Clinical psychology focuses on diagnosing and treating psychological disorders and other problematic patterns of behavior.
Cognitive psychology studies thoughts and mental processes and their relationship to experience and action.
Developmental psychology is the scientific study of development across the lifespan.
Social psychology focuses on how people interact with and relate to others.
Biological psychology explores how biology, especially the nervous system, influences behavior.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Is psychology a natural science or a social science?
positions: Behavior is at its roots biological, so some areas of psychology work like a natural science (OpenStax 1.1)
People are shaped by interactions with others, so psychology is also a social science (OpenStax 1.1)
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson presents both: psychology straddles the natural and social sciences, which is why it spans biological and social subfields.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Can the mind be studied scientifically when it cannot be observed directly?
positions: The mind is not directly observable; thoughts as experienced are neither matter nor energy (OpenStax 1.1)
Behaviorists historically excluded mental activity as unsuitable for scientific study (APA behavior entry)
Modern psychology studies the mind indirectly through measurable indicators such as self-report and behavior (APA mind entry)
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states that psychology studies both mind and behavior, with the mind approached through measurable indicators, and notes the honest limit that some inner experience is not yet directly measurable.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Pop psychology claims versus research-backed claims
positions: Popular claims can match everyday experience yet lack systematic testing (lesson synthesis; OpenStax 1.1 on a world full of competing 'facts')
Research findings must survive clear questions, measured outcomes, peer review, and replication (OpenStax 1.1 on the scientific method)
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson distinguishes the two by evidence and presents psychology as rigorous about evidence and humble about certainty.

sourceRecords.title: APA Dictionary of Psychology — Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A. Entry defines psychology as 'the scientific study of the mind and behavior' and describes it as emerging from philosophy into an empirical science spanning research and applied branches. Read via the dictionary's public JSON API (getdopdefinitions?q=psychology) because the site renders content client-side; URL field is the canonical public entry. Definitional facts used; no wording reproduced.

sourceRecords.title: APA Dictionary of Psychology — Mind
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A. Entry defines mind broadly as all intellectual and psychological phenomena of an organism and narrowly as cognitive activities such as perceiving, attending, thinking, problem solving, language, learning, and memory. Read via the dictionary's public JSON API. Supports the mind–behavior distinction.

sourceRecords.title: APA Dictionary of Psychology — Behavior
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A. Entry defines behavior as an organism's activities in response to internal or external stimuli, including objectively observable activities, covert activities, and nonconscious processes. Read via the dictionary's public JSON API. Supports the mind–behavior distinction.

sourceRecords.title: OpenStax Psychology 2e, Section 1.1: What Is Psychology?
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A open textbook. Canonical openstax.org URL registered; openstax.org blocks direct fetch, so the page was read via Internet Archive snapshot 20260724084832. Supports: psychology as the scientific study of the mind and behavior; psychologists using the scientific method; science working with what is perceivable and measurable; psychology becoming its own academic discipline in the late 1800s; psychology as both natural and social science; critical thinking in a world of competing 'facts'.

sourceRecords.title: OpenStax Psychology 2e, Section 1.3: Contemporary Psychology
sourceRecords.notes: Tier A open textbook. Canonical openstax.org URL registered; read via Internet Archive snapshot 20260801175018. Supplies the one-line descriptions of the five subfields: clinical (diagnosis and treatment of psychological disorders and problematic behavior patterns), cognitive (thoughts and mental processes and their relation to experience and action), developmental (scientific study of development across the lifespan), social (how we interact with and relate to others), and biopsychology (how biology, especially the nervous system, influences behavior).

sourceRecords.title: Simply Psychology — What Is Psychology?
sourceRecords.notes: Tier B. Corroborates the APA attribution of the working definition (psychology as the scientific study of the mind and behavior) and the historical point that psychology is a comparatively new science whose origins are philosophical. Used only as supporting corroboration alongside the Tier A anchors; no wording reproduced.
